fca.command: python main.py dataset=mvtec fe=wide sc=fca image_size=original tile_size=[9,9]
fca.feature_extractor: WideResnetExtractor(post_scale=True): WideResNet-50-2 up to layer2 (512 channels, stride 8), per-channel min-max scaling
fca.sc: ScFCA(tile_size=[9,9], chunk_size=8, sigma_p=3.0, reference_selection=median, k_s=5, sigma_s=1.0) (conf/sc/fca.yaml)
fca.reason: the official full-resolution setting (README and paper Table 6); kept unchanged

aota.command_equivalent: python main.py dataset=mvtec fe=wide sc=aota image_size=[320,320] tile_size=[3,3]
aota.feature_extractor: WideResnetExtractor(post_scale=True), the same as for FCA
aota.sc: sc_aota(tile_size=[3,3], sigma=100.0, k=400) (conf/sc/aota.yaml passes tile_size; sigma and k are code defaults)
aota.map_resolution: 320x320 (40x40 feature grid = 1600 patches, scored, then resized to 320x320 and smoothed)
reasons: Aota et al. (WACV 2023) as stated in the instruction: WideResNet-50 block 2, resize 320x320, 3x3 local average pooling, K=400 nearest neighbours out of 1600 patches, Gaussian sigma 4, 256x256 centre crop.
FCA paper: its 320x320 variant uses T=3 for consistency with Aota (Sec. 3.4 / App. D.2).
The earlier choice tile_size=[9,9] was only the repo default in conf/base.yaml; it was replaced by [3,3] before any aota result was computed.
aota.sigma_100_explained: In sc_aota, sigma=100 is the std (in feature-grid cells) of the Gaussian in op_utils.blur(features, kernel_size=tile_size[0], sigma=100), applied to the 40x40 feature map. With kernel size 3 a Gaussian of std 100 is flat: measured 1-D weights 0.333328-0.333344 (uniform 1/3); repo blur vs 3x3 average pooling (stride 1, reflect padding) max |diff| 1.35e-05 on random features. So sigma=100 implements the paper's 3x3 local average pooling; it is NOT the paper's Gaussian sigma 4.
aota.paper_sigma_4: corresponds to the last line of sc_aota: blur(F.interpolate(score, (320,320)), kernel_size=25, sigma=4.0), a Gaussian of std 4 px on the 320x320 output map (measured 1-D weights 0.0011-0.0999, i.e. a real Gaussian). Units: pixels of the 320x320 map. This matches the paper's Gaussian sigma 4 if the paper smooths the 320x320 map (stated as such in the instruction; not checked against the Aota paper text here).
aota.k_400: code default k=400: mean of the 400 smallest squared L2 distances from each patch to all 1600 patches of the same image (includes the patch itself, distance 0), matching K=400 of 1600.
aota.centre_crop_256: sc_aota does not crop. A 256x256 centre crop of a 320x320 map removes 32 px = 10% per side; the crop10 version of the metrics (52 of 518 px = 10% per side) corresponds to it. The full version is reported as well.
aota.estimate_note: the timing estimate was run with tile_size [9,9] (0.28 s/image); it is used only for the time estimate

evaluation_grid: all maps resized to 518x518 (bilinear, cv2.INTER_LINEAR) to match the 518x518 NEAREST ground-truth masks of src/eval_router_full.py
crop10: 52 px removed on every side of the 518x518 map and mask; image labels from the cropped mask (as the repo's evaluate_experiment.py)
